born.why: The code improves safety by using trait-based inference (color/shape similarity) to guess if an unknown fruit is safe or poisonous based on past experiences with similar fruits, rather than treating each species in isolation.

This code improves survival by prioritizing starvation avoidance, then using trait-based generalization (inferring safety from similar known-safe fruits) to reduce unnecessary tasting risks while still allowing learning of new species.
The code prioritizes avoiding known poisons and starving, then uses 'taste' for unknown targets or exploratory finds to gain information with minimal risk, only eating whole when safe and hungry.

The code prioritizes species-specific memory over trait inference for safety, uses trait matching only as a secondary filter for unknown fruits to avoid false positives from benign shared traits, and dynamically balances risk-taking based on hunger levels to ensure survival while maximizing data collection.
The code prioritizes survival by eating when hunger is critical, learns via tasting when safe to do so, and stores known-safe fruits for later use to maximize long-term energy efficiency.

The code prioritizes survival by using trait-based inference for unknown fruits, avoiding those sharing traits with past poisons unless starving, and efficiently managing inventory by carrying only when the pantry is low.

This code improves survival by distinguishing between critical starvation (eat anything) and moderate hunger (taste unknowns), while prioritizing carrying known safe food to the pantry when not immediately starving to build a safety reserve for future crises.
